fairUse.provenance: Rendered page 1 of the official publisher rules PDF https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0740/4855/files/ONUW_Getting_Started_for_BGG.pdf. The illustrated title page visibly identifies this game and matches the linked rules edition; reduced to 274 × 360 pixels for display.

firstPlayerRule: There is no first player. At night, roles wake up in a fixed order called out by the Announcer (one designated player) or by the free app; during the day, everyone discusses freely and then all players vote at the same time.
clarifications: Roles with a night action are called in the order set by the rules (the numbers on the role tokens show the wake order).
The guide says one player is designated the Announcer but gives no method for choosing that player; the app can replace the Announcer.

internalEvidence: Downloaded the Getting Started Guide linked from the Bezier Games product page (https://beziergames.com/products/one-night-ultimate-werewolf), SHA-256 16b053afb9243aa15b2f1c59078acb6522983300f426648b11e982e63c7895ed. The PDF has no text layer, so all 4 pages were rendered and read visually. Page 2, Night: one player is designated the Announcer and announces each role in order, with a sample script. Page 3, Day: players discuss, then on 'Everyone, three, two, one, VOTE!' each player points to another player; the free app can replace the Announcer; role token numbers correspond to the night wake order. Also checked the role rulebook linked from the same page (ONUW_rules-updated_for_BGG.pdf, SHA-256 3ed5be0765f50779139a4cec7dd765ded77a1d68cc6473c919375b9a067986a4), pages 2-3, which describes role wake order only. The werewolf social-deduction game with one night and one day matches BGG 147949. No copyright year was visible in the guide. Owner authorized assistant review on 2026-09-25. Editorial review 2026-09-25: Rechecked the source pages, opening instruction, game identity, and edition.
uncertainty: The guide does not say how to choose the Announcer.
